q: Using the bound h ≤ 2·log₂(n + 1), what is the largest height that a red-black tree with 15 internal nodes could have?
explain:
h ≤ 2·log₂(15 + 1) = 2·log₂ 16 = 2 × 4 = 8

The bound comes from n ≥ 2^bh − 1 and bh ≥ h/2. (Real trees with 15 keys are usually much shorter. The bound is a worst-case guarantee.)

q: Keys 50, 40, 30, 20, 10 are inserted, in that order, into an initially empty red-black tree (standard insertion with recolouring and rotations). How many red nodes does the final tree have?
explain:
insert 50        → 50B
insert 40        → 50B, 40R as its left child
insert 30        → red-red, uncle NIL (black), outer: rotate right at 50
                   → 40B with children 30R, 50R
insert 20        → parent 30R, uncle 50R: recolour → 30B, 50B, 40 stays B (root)
insert 10        → parent 20R, uncle NIL (black), outer: rotate right at 30
                   → 20B with children 10R, 30R
final: 40B ( 20B (10R, 30R), 50B )

Two red nodes: 10 and 30.

q: Which statements about red-black trees are true?
options: An insertion performs at most two rotations
Every red-black tree satisfies the AVL balance condition
Both children of a red node are black
The root may be red if the tree has only one node
explain:
(A) is true: only the final case-2/case-3 fix rotates. (C) is rule 4.

(B) is false. A red-black tree can have subtree heights differing by more than one; it only guarantees longest path ≤ 2 × shortest. (D) is false: the root is always black, which the fix-up enforces as its last step.

q: In a red-black tree, every path from the root down to a NIL leaf contains exactly 3 black internal nodes (the root included, NIL leaves not counted). What is the largest number of internal nodes such a path can contain?
explain:
The 3 black nodes are fixed. Red nodes can only be squeezed in where they do not touch another red: at most one red directly below each black node. (A red right above a NIL leaf is fine, because NIL leaves are black.)

root(B) → R → B → R → B → R → NIL
black internal nodes: 3     red nodes: 3     total: 6

The root must be black, so no red can come before it. That gives a maximum of 3 + 3 = 6, which is exactly the factor of 2 behind the bound h ≤ 2·log₂(n + 1).
